title: AI systems are fully capable of carrying out nightmare attacks against infrastructure and nobody's ready
key_facts: Booz Allen Hamilton's operational technology (OT) lab tested eight scenarios of an autonomous, AI-enabled attack on OT and industrial equipment; the models achieved the objectives across all eight.
In one case an agent found and moved a robotic arm within minutes; in another, the models went from a perimeter compromise to actions inside an industrial control network in just over 16 minutes.
Booz Allen declined to name the two 'latest frontier models' it tested; the models were given no source code, engineering documents or advanced OT or IT guidance.
Guardrails: agents had to wait for human approval before exploiting a security issue or taking any action that could cause a physical impact.
The lab mimicked a general manufacturing facility with mixed vendors, controllers (PLCs), a SCADA platform, a variable-frequency drive, a robotic arm and sensors.
Kyle Miller of Booz Allen says defenders may have only minutes to detect and block such an attack and that specialised OT knowledge is no longer a real barrier.
Booz Allen wants more industry testing and more deployment of defences across OT and critical infrastructure networks.

The Register links the research to reports of suspected Chinese operators using AI agents against South Korean financial institutions and suspected Iranian attackers using AI-generated scripts against US water, manufacturing and energy controllers.
quote_evidence: The consulting firm's operational technology (OT) lab tested eight scenarios to examine advanced models' capabilities within an autonomous, AI-enabled OT attack chain.
Agents had to wait for human approval before exploiting a security issue or taking any action that could cause a physical impact.
In another test, the models progressed from a perimeter compromise to actions inside an industrial control network in just over 16 minutes.
why_it_matters_hint: A consulting firm's lab test suggests AI agents can reach industrial control systems quickly, but it was a simulated plant with unnamed models and human sign-off.
notes: Single outlet (The Register) reporting a company's own lab test; models unnamed, no outside review reported. Booz Allen's report itself was not opened.
